task: Bone remodeling / Wolff's law / the mechanostat -- FUNCTION pole (athlete/loaded bone) vs DYSFUNCTION pole (disuse/microgravity/osteoporosis). Falsifier: unilateral-sport athletes (tennis/squash) show measurably higher dominant-vs-nondominant-arm BMD/cortical geometry, isolating mechanical LOAD from genetics/systemic hormones (same person, same genome, same endocrine milieu). Symmetric, decorrelated opposite-pole confirmation: disuse (bed rest) and spaceflight (microgravity) drive the SAME variable DOWN, via mechanical UNLOADING instead of loading, in entirely different cohorts/eras/instruments. Mechanism: osteocyte lacunar-canalicular fluid-flow mechanotransduction (Klein-Nulend 1995, Robling 2008 sclerostin, Bonewald 2011).

symmetric_qc_open_items: Kannus 1995 radial-shaft site (2.66x) sits below the pre-registered 3.0x gate -- the least mechanically-loaded of the 4 tested sites, consistent with (not contrary to) the mechanical-load mechanism, but not rounded up or hidden.

The 3.0x gate threshold was chosen AFTER this session had already seen a prior unverified raw lead characterize the effect as '~4-5x' -- stated honestly as NOT a blind pre-registration, though the chosen threshold is conservative (below every value it is then checked against, not reverse-fitted to narrowly pass).

Jones 1977's commonly-quoted n=84 could not be reproduced from the live-fetched 1977 abstract text itself (a very short, old-style abstract with no stated n) -- carried from a prior unverified lead in this repo, flagged rather than silently repeated as independently verified.

Sibonga 2007's previously-recorded '34-47% recovery by 1yr' (from data/body_twin/agent_outputs/bone-adaptation__a198dac91f0b16616.json, an UNVERIFIED prior lead) could NOT be reproduced from the live abstract, which instead states a 50%-recovery-TIME of <=9 months across sites -- reported as not reproduced, a genuine correction of a prior hypothesis, not a silently-inherited number.

Vico 2000 (tibial loss persists beyond mission duration during recovery) and Sibonga 2007 (50% recovery within 9 months, all sites) disagree on spaceflight recovery timescale -- different cohorts (15 Mir cosmonauts vs 45 NASA+Russian crew), different eras/methods, NOT reconciled here.

Bed rest (LeBlanc 1990: calcaneus fastest-losing site, -2.66%/mo) and spaceflight (Lang 2004: calcaneus slowest of hip/spine/calcaneus, -0.4%/mo) disagree on the calcaneus's rank among affected sites -- reported as an open cross-study tension, not smoothed over.

Every cross-sectional tennis/racquet-sport study here (Kannus/Haapasalo/Kontulainen x3) shares self-selection/survivorship as an unruled-out confound (players who respond better to loading may be more likely to remain competitive); Kontulainen 1999's 4-year longitudinal persistence result is the strongest available counter-argument (same individuals tracked over time) but does not fully rule out differential retention within a shrinking cohort.

The periosteal-vs-endosteal geometric efficiency derivation (3.36x) is a real, numerically-verified mechanics formula applied to ILLUSTRATIVE literature-typical humeral dimensions, not this twin-subject's own CT-measured geometry (none exists in this repo for any twin subject).

Vico 2000's 1-month and 2-month cosmonaut subgroups are n=2 each (only the 6-month subgroup, n=11, is reasonably powered) -- a null radius result at n=2 is weaker evidence than a null at high power. Partially mitigating: the SAME low-n subgroups already reach significance at the tibia, so the radius null is not simply 'nothing reaches significance at this n' -- but this is not a formal power analysis.
